chunks: And by this isnad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, from his father, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever gives one carat to someone from my Ahl al-Bayt in this worldly life, I will recompense him on the Day of Resurrection with a qintar.

key_terms.أهل البيت: The Prophet's household; a central concept in Shia theology referring to the Prophet, Fatimah, and the twelve Imams
key_terms.قنطار: A qintar — a large unit of weight (100 ritl or more), signifying an immense divine reward
key_terms.قيراط: A carat — a small unit of weight, signifying even a minimal act of charity or support
key_terms.يوم القيامة: The Day of Resurrection, when all deeds are accounted for

ai.seo_question: What reward does the Prophet promise for supporting the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) promises that whoever gives even a minimal gift (a carat's worth) to a member of his household in this world will receive an immense reward (a qintar) on the Day of Resurrection. This teaching underscores the immense spiritual merit of honoring and supporting the Ahl al-Bayt, and reflects the Shia theological emphasis on the Prophet's family as central to piety and salvation.
